name: Sigüenza Cathedral
story: In the autumn of 1936 Nationalist columns advancing from Aragon and Soria besieged Sigüenza. The last Republican militiamen, with civilians, took refuge in the cathedral and held out for several days under artillery and air bombardment before surrendering in mid-October. The cathedral suffered heavy damage: roofs and the crossing collapsed, sculpture was shattered and the 18th-century organ destroyed. It was restored in the 1940s, when a new lantern tower was added over the crossing.
see: The fortress-like Romanesque–Gothic cathedral, restored; post-war repairs and the new lantern are visible.
plan: Cathedral open daily; the €10 ticket covers the cathedral and diocesan museum (self-guided). Sigüenza is 1 h 45 min from Madrid by train.
